title: Spaghetti carbonara
intro: Just eggs, crisp guanciale and pecorino, made silky with pasta water.

steps.t: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and salt it lightly: guanciale and pecorino are already salty.
Cut the guanciale into strips and fry it in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and crisp.
steps.label: Guanciale

steps.t: Meanwhile, whisk the yolks, egg, pecorino and plenty of ground pepper in a bowl into a thick cream.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente.
steps.label: Spaghetti

steps.t: Drain, keeping a ladle of pasta water, and tip the pasta into the guanciale pan with the heat off.
Add the egg cream and toss fast, loosening with pasta water until creamy, not scrambled.
Serve right away with more pecorino and a grind of pepper.

tips.t: If the pan is still very hot, toss pasta and egg cream in the bowl instead so the egg won't scramble.
No guanciale? Unsmoked pancetta works; cream and garlic don't belong here.

title: Bucatini all’amatriciana
intro: Guanciale, tomato and pecorino: the Amatrice classic, no onion.

steps.t: Cut the guanciale into strips and fry it with the chili until the fat turns clear and golden.
steps.label: Guanciale

steps.t: Splash in the wine, let it evaporate, then lift out half the guanciale and keep it crisp.
Add the tomatoes crushed by hand, salt lightly and simmer over medium heat until the sauce thickens.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Meanwhile, cook the bucatini in salted water and drain them al dente.
steps.label: Bucatini

steps.t: Toss the pasta in the sauce with a splash of pasta water and the reserved guanciale.
Turn off the heat, stir in the pecorino and serve with an extra sprinkle.

tips.t: Add the reserved guanciale only at the end so it stays crisp instead of going soft in the sauce.
Leave out the tomato and you have gricia, its ancestor.

title: Cacio e pepe
intro: Three ingredients and a pecorino cream bound by the starch in the pasta water.

steps.t: Crush the pepper coarsely and toast it in a dry wide pan until fragrant.
steps.label: Pepper

steps.t: Cook the pasta in a small amount of lightly salted water so it stays starchy.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: Meanwhile, work the pecorino in a bowl with a little cooled pasta water into a smooth paste.
Pour a ladle of pasta water over the pepper and add the pasta, drained al dente.
With the heat off, add the pecorino cream and stir hard until it binds.
If it's too thick, loosen with water; serve at once with pepper and pecorino.

tips.t: Never let the pecorino hit a hot pan: above 65 °C it turns lumpy.
Swap a third of the pecorino for Parmigiano: the sauce is milder and binds more easily.

title: Rigatoni alla gricia
intro: The ancestor of amatriciana: guanciale, pecorino and pepper, no tomato.

steps.t: Cut the guanciale into strips and fry it without oil over medium heat until golden but still tender inside.
steps.label: Guanciale

steps.t: Cook the rigatoni in lightly salted water.
steps.label: Rigatoni

steps.t: Meanwhile, lift out half the guanciale, add a ladle of pasta water to the pan and swirl to emulsify the fat.
Drain the pasta al dente and toss it in the pan for a minute.
Turn off the heat, add pecorino and pepper and stir until the sauce turns creamy.
Serve topped with the reserved guanciale.

tips.t: Stir in a cream of yolks and pecorino and it becomes carbonara.
Crush the pepper in a mortar right before using: pre-ground pepper has lost its aroma.

title: Spaghetti aglio, olio e peperoncino
intro: The midnight pasta: a few minutes, good oil and barely golden garlic.

steps.t: Cook the spaghetti in plenty of salted water.
steps.label: Spaghetti

steps.t: Meanwhile, slice the garlic thinly and crumble the chilies.
Warm the oil over low heat with garlic and chili until the garlic is just golden, never burnt.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: Add a ladle of pasta water to the oil and shake the pan to emulsify.
Drain the spaghetti al dente and toss them in the pan for a minute with the parsley.
Serve at once with a drizzle of raw oil.

tips.t: Start the garlic in cold oil: it colours slowly and never turns bitter.
Finish with breadcrumbs toasted in a pan for the crunch of southern Italian home cooking.

title: Trofie with Genoese pesto
intro: The Ligurian way: potatoes and green beans cooked with the pasta, raw pesto.

steps.t: Peel and dice the potatoes; trim the green beans and cut them into 3 cm pieces.
Drop potatoes and beans into boiling salted water.
steps.label: Veg

steps.t: Add the trofie to the same pot and cook until al dente.
steps.label: Trofie

steps.t: Meanwhile, loosen the pesto (good shop-bought is fine) in a large bowl with 2–3 tbsp of pasta water.
Drain pasta and vegetables and toss them with the pesto without heating it, so the basil stays green.
Serve with Parmigiano and a basil leaf.

tips.t: Never heat pesto in a pan: heat darkens the basil and makes it bitter.
Trenette or flat silk-handkerchief pasta are just as Ligurian.

title: Spaghetti alla puttanesca
intro: Olives, capers and anchovies: Naples' boldest store-cupboard sauce.

steps.t: Warm the oil with crushed garlic, chili and anchovies over low heat until the anchovies melt.
steps.label: Anchovies

steps.t: Add the pitted olives and rinsed capers and let them sizzle for a minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer over medium heat until the sauce thickens.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in lightly salted water.
steps.label: Spaghetti

steps.t: Drain al dente and toss in the sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Remove the garlic, scatter with parsley and serve.

tips.t: Taste before salting: anchovies, olives and capers bring all the salt you need.
Skip the anchovies and add a few extra capers for a vegan version.

title: Pasta alla Norma
intro: Fried aubergine, tomato sauce and ricotta salata: a Catania summer on a plate.

steps.t: Dice the aubergines, salt them and leave them in a colander to release their water.
steps.label: Aubergine

steps.t: Rinse quickly and pat them very dry with kitchen paper.
Fry in batches in oil at 170 °C until golden; drain on paper.
steps.label: Frying

oven.t: Toss with 3 tbsp oil and roast at 200 °C for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.

airfryer.t: Toss with 1 tbsp oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 15 minutes, shaking halfway.

steps.t: Cook the pasta in salted water.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: Meanwhile, warm the tomato sauce (homemade or shop-bought) with a few basil leaves.
Drain the pasta al dente and toss it in the sauce with half the aubergine.
Serve topped with the rest of the aubergine, grated ricotta salata and basil.

tips.t: Fry a few pieces at a time: if the oil cools, the aubergine soaks it up and goes soggy.
No ricotta salata? Use a young pecorino, grated coarsely.

title: Pasta e broccoli
intro: Neapolitan style: the pasta cooks with the broccoli and turns creamy on its own.

steps.t: Cut the broccoli into small florets and dice the peeled stalk.
In a pot, fry the garlic and chili in the oil for a minute without burning them.
Add the broccoli, a pinch of salt and 1 litre of boiling water; cook until tender.
steps.label: Broccoli

steps.t: Mash part of the broccoli with a wooden spoon to make a cream.
Add the pasta straight to the pot and cook, stirring, adding a splash of hot water if needed.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: It should be thick and creamy, not soupy: turn off the heat and let it rest.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve with a drizzle of raw olive oil.

tips.t: It's even better the next day: fry it in a pan with a little oil until it forms a crust.
Off the heat, stir in diced provola: it melts into strings and makes it rich (no longer vegan).

title: Pasta alla crudaiola
intro: Raw marinated cherry tomatoes and basil: hot pasta makes the sauce for you.

steps.t: Quarter the cherry tomatoes and put them in a large bowl.
Dress them with oil, crushed garlic, oregano, salt and torn basil, then leave to marinate.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Meanwhile, cook the pasta in salted water.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: Meanwhile, fish the garlic out of the tomatoes and tear more basil.
Drain the pasta al dente and tip it hot into the bowl: toss until it soaks up the juices.
Serve warm or at room temperature, with more basil.

tips.t: Add diced mozzarella or feta at the end for a summer one-bowl meal (no longer vegan).
The longer the tomatoes sit, the more juice they give: you can prep them an hour ahead.

title: Pumpkin, rosemary and hazelnut pasta
intro: Pumpkin cooked down into its own cream, with toasted hazelnuts for crunch.

steps.t: Dice the pumpkin and finely chop the onion.
Soften the onion in the oil with the rosemary over medium heat.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the pumpkin, salt it, pour in a glass of water and cook over medium heat until it falls apart.
steps.label: Pumpkin

steps.t: Meanwhile, toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan and chop them roughly.
Cook the pasta in salted water.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: Meanwhile, remove the rosemary and mash half the pumpkin with a fork into a cream.
Drain the pasta al dente and toss it with the pumpkin and a ladle of pasta water.
Serve with the hazelnuts, pepper and a drizzle of raw olive oil.

tips.t: A grating of nutmeg or a pinch of chili brings out the pumpkin's sweetness.
Fry crumbled sausage with the onion for a heartier dish (no longer vegan).

title: Pasta con le sarde
intro: Sardines, wild fennel, raisins and pine nuts: Palermo's sweet-savoury classic.

steps.t: Soak the raisins in warm water.
steps.label: Raisins

steps.t: Meanwhile, boil the fennel in plenty of salted water, drain it keeping the water, and chop it.
steps.label: Fennel

steps.t: Toast the breadcrumbs in a pan with 1 tbsp oil until golden; set aside.
Fry the chopped onion in the remaining oil with the anchovies until soft and the anchovies melt.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add sardine pieces, squeezed raisins, pine nuts, fennel and saffron dissolved in a little water; cook over medium heat.
steps.label: Sardines

steps.t: Meanwhile, cook the bucatini in the fennel water, which perfumes them.
steps.label: Bucatini

steps.t: Drain al dente and toss in the sauce with a ladle of pasta water.
Serve topped with the toasted breadcrumbs instead of cheese.

tips.t: In Sicily, fish pasta gets no cheese: toasted breadcrumbs take its place.
No wild fennel? Use the fronds of two fennel bulbs plus a pinch of fennel seeds.

title: Spaghetti alle vongole
intro: Clams opened in the pan, with spaghetti finished in their juices.

steps.t: Purge the clams in cold salted water (35 g salt per litre), changing the water halfway.
steps.label: Purge

steps.t: Drain them and discard any that are broken, or open and don't close when tapped.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water, 2 minutes less than the packet says.
steps.label: Spaghetti

steps.t: Meanwhile, heat the oil with garlic and chili, add the clams, splash in the wine and cover until they open.
steps.label: Clams

steps.t: Remove the garlic and a few empty shells; discard any clams that stayed shut.
Drain the spaghetti and finish cooking them in the clam juices, stirring often.
steps.label: Finish

steps.t: Turn off the heat, add parsley and a drizzle of raw oil and serve at once.

tips.t: If grit settles in the pan, strain the juices through a fine sieve before adding the pasta.
Pour a crisp white from Campania, such as Falanghina.

title: Chickpea pasta with cavolo nero
intro: Pure chickpea pasta, sautéed cavolo nero, lemon and almonds: gluten-free.

steps.t: Strip the central rib from the cavolo nero and cut the leaves into thin ribbons.
Blanch the leaves in the salted pasta water, then lift them out with a slotted spoon.
steps.label: Kale

steps.t: Cook the chickpea pasta in the same water, keeping it al dente as it breaks easily.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: Meanwhile, fry sliced garlic in the oil with the chili, then add the kale and sauté for 3 minutes.
Drain the pasta gently and add it to the kale with a splash of pasta water.
Finish with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice and the roughly chopped almonds.

tips.t: Chickpea pasta foams a lot: use a large pot and leave the lid off.
Red lentil pasta works too and tastes a little sweeter.

title: Pasta with asparagus and lemon
intro: Stalks cooked to a cream, just-crisp tips and lemon zest: spring in a bowl.

steps.t: Snap off the woody ends of the asparagus, cut off the tips and slice the stalks into rounds.
Cook the pasta in salted water.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: Meanwhile, soften the chopped shallot in the butter, then add the stalks and cook over medium heat.
steps.label: Stalks

steps.t: Add the tips and a ladle of pasta water and cook until tender but still green.
steps.label: Tips

steps.t: Drain the pasta al dente and toss with the asparagus, lemon zest and a squeeze of juice.
Off the heat, stir in Parmigiano and pasta water until creamy; serve with pepper and more zest.

tips.t: Boil the woody ends in the pasta water: they give it an asparagus aroma.
Add sautéed prawns at the end for a springtime seafood pasta.

title: Spaghetti alla Nerano
intro: Fried courgettes and provolone melted into a cream: Amalfi Coast summer.

steps.t: Slice the courgettes into thin rounds.
Fry them in batches in oil at 170 °C until golden; drain on paper and salt them.
steps.label: Courgettes

steps.t: Put them in a bowl with torn basil and let them rest: they turn soft.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in salted water, 2 minutes less than the packet says.
steps.label: Spaghetti

steps.t: Put half the courgettes in a pan with a ladle of pasta water and crush them a little.
Drain the spaghetti into the pan, turn off the heat and add the grated cheeses bit by bit with pasta water.
Stir until creamy, add the remaining courgettes, pepper and basil and serve.

tips.t: Fry the courgettes the day before: resting in the fridge makes them softer and tastier.
No Provolone del Monaco? Use mild provolone plus a spoonful of pecorino.

title: Mac and cheese
intro: Macaroni in a stretchy cheddar sauce, baked under a crunchy crumb top.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C and cook the macaroni in salted water, 2 minutes less than the packet says.
steps.label: Macaroni

steps.t: Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan, add the flour and stir for a minute without letting it colour.
Whisk in the milk gradually and cook over medium heat until the sauce coats the spoon.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Turn off the heat and stir in mustard, three quarters of the cheddar, salt and pepper until smooth.
Drain the pasta, mix it into the sauce and pour into a baking dish.
Top with the remaining cheddar, breadcrumbs and paprika and bake until golden and bubbling at the edges.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Let it rest for a few minutes before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Swap a third of the cheddar for Gruyère, or scatter crisp bacon on top.
Next day, cut it into squares and fry them in a pan until crusty.

title: Koshari
intro: Cairo's street dish: lentils, rice and pasta with spicy sauce and crispy onions.

steps.t: Simmer the lentils in unsalted water until tender but whole; salt at the end and drain.
steps.label: Lentils

steps.t: Meanwhile, slice the onions thinly and fry them in the oil over medium heat until dark and crisp; drain on paper.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Toast the rice for a minute in 2 tbsp of the onion oil, add 300 ml salted water and cook covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Meanwhile, cook the pasta in salted water and drain.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: For the sauce, fry chopped garlic in 1 tbsp oil with cumin and chili, then add passata and salt.
Simmer the sauce over medium heat until thick and finish with the vinegar.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Warm the rinsed chickpeas in a small pan with a splash of water.
Plate up: rice, lentils and pasta mixed, then sauce, chickpeas and lots of crispy onions.

tips.t: Fry the onions patiently over medium heat until almost black but not burnt: they make the dish.
Serve a 'dakka' on the side: garlic, vinegar, cumin and water, spooned over to taste.
